You see, the micro:bit is stored as a string of 25 bits of either 0 (dark) or 1 (light) per bit. Splitting the 25 bits into chunks of 5, each chunk is a row. The first 5 is the top row from left-to-right, then the next 5 (6th to 10th bit) is the row between the top and the middle from left-to-right (horizontally), and then so on and so forth until the last 5 series of 0s and/or 1s shows the light for the last row. There is a website dedicated to checking if passwords have been seen in data breaches (not made by me). It is at haveibeenpwned.com. of times your password has been found in a data breach indexed on that site. This is because the hash is stored on the client's computer, and only the first part gets sent. ...(or ' in the actual webpage).
